extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, licensees, opponents, agents, and Patent Office / Board of Trade officials (United Kingdom, 1890)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and documentary requirements for prosecution, amendment, renewal, compulsory licences, register entries, forms, and fees under the Patents Rules (UK, 1890). Targets applicants, patentees, opponents, licensees, and Patent Office officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of annual/renewal fees and certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patentee intends to pay annual fees in lieu of specified lump fees, he shall before the expiration of the fourth and each succeeding year during the term of the patent, until and inclusive of the thirteenth year, pay the prescribed fee. On due compliance the Comptroller shall issue a certificate that the prescribed payment has been duly made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form J for payment/certificate. Comptroller enters payment record in the Register upon issue of certificate (see Rule 75). Failure to make prescribed payment within prescribed time (or enlargement) is to be entered in the register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for enlargement of time for payment of prescribed fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for an enlargement of time for payment must state in detail the circumstances in which the patentee by accident, mistake, or inadvertence has failed to make such payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Comptroller may require the patentee to substantiate allegations by such proof as he thinks necessary. See Form K for application format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for enlargement of time for leaving or accepting a complete specification
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for enlargement of time for leaving or accepting a complete specification shall state in detail in what circumstances, and upon what grounds, such extension is applied for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Comptroller may require the applicant to substantiate such allegations by such proof as the Comptroller may think necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller's discretion to enlarge prescribed time
rubrics_metrics.description: The time prescribed by the Rules for doing any act or taking any proceeding thereunder may be enlarged by the Comptroller if he think fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enlargement may be subject to such notice to other parties, proceedings thereon, and terms as the Comptroller may direct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for leave to amend a specification (form & publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for leave to amend a specification must be signed by the applicant or patentee and accompanied by a duly certified printed copy of the original specification and drawings, showing in red ink the proposed amendment, and shall be advertised by publication of the request and the nature of the proposed amendment in the official journal of the Patent Office and in such other manner as the Comptroller may direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form F for the application to amend; ensure red-ink markings clearly show proposed changes; comply with advertisement requirements directed by Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of opposition to amendment — content & form
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of opposition to the amendment shall state the ground or grounds on which the opponent intends to oppose the amendment and must be signed by him; it shall state his address for service in the United Kingdom and be accompanied by an unstamped copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form G gives the form of this notice. Provide a UK address for service and an unstamped copy for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller to transmit copy of opposition to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of such notice a copy thereof shall be transmitted by the Comptroller to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely transmission enables the applicant to respond and prepare any affidavits/statutory declarations required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opponent may file statutory declarations in support of opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 14 days after the expiration of one month from the first advertisement of the application for leave to amend, the opponent may leave at the Patent Office statutory declarations in support of his opposition and on so leaving shall deliver to the applicant a list thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the statutory declarations within the 14-day window following the one-month advertisement period; deliver a list of declarations to applicant concurrently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further proceedings on opposition governed by earlier rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon such declarations being left, and such list being delivered, the provisions of Rules 38, 39, 40, 41, and 44 shall apply to the case, and further proceedings shall be regulated accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Rules 38–41 and 44 for detailed procedural steps (e.g., service, affidavit procedures, hearing steps) once declarations are filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file amended specification and drawings after leave
rubrics_metrics.description: Where leave to amend is given the applicant shall, if the Comptroller so require, and within a time to be limited by him, leave at the Patent Office a new specification and drawings as amended, to be prepared in accordance with Rules 10, 30, and 31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare amended complete specification and drawings complying with the referenced formatting and content rules; file within the time limit set by Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave to amend pursuant to court order requires verified copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for leave to amend is made by or in pursuance of an order of the Court or a judge, an official or verified copy of the order shall be left with the request at the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach a certified/verified copy of the court order when filing the request to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement of every amendment by Comptroller
rubrics_metrics.description: Every amendment of a specification shall be forthwith advertised by the Comptroller in the official journal of the Patent Office and in such other manner as the Comptroller may direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect publication in the Official Journal; Comptroller may require additional publicity measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for compulsory licence — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to the Board of Trade for an order upon a patentee to grant a licence shall show clearly the nature of the petitioner's interest, and the ground or grounds upon which he claims to be entitled to relief, and shall state in detail the circumstances of the case, the terms upon which he asks that an order may be made, and the purport of such order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the petitioner’s interest, factual circumstances, grounds under section 22 (or applicable provision), and proposed licence terms clearly and in detail. Use Form H/I as guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing petition and supporting evidence for compulsory licence
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition and an examined copy thereof shall be left at the Patent Office, accompanied by the affidavits or statutory declarations, and other documentary evidence, if any, tendered by the petitioner in proof of the alleged default of the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File an examined (certified) copy of the petition plus all supporting affidavits/declarations and documentary evidence with the Patent Office when lodging the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Trade may require petitioner attendance and give directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon perusal and evidence, unless the Board of Trade shall be of opinion that the order should be at once refused, they may require the petitioner to attend before the Comptroller, or other person or persons appointed by them, to receive directions as to further proceedings upon the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to attend before the Comptroller or appointed person to receive procedural directions; Board may direct further evidence or steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to deliver copies to patentee when prima facie case made
rubrics_metrics.description: If and when a prima-facie case for relief has been made out to the satisfaction of the Board of Trade, the petitioner shall upon their requisition, and on or before a day to be named by them, deliver to the patentee copies of the petition, and of the affidavits or statutory declarations and other documentary evidence tendered in support thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Board so requires, serve the patentee with full copies of petition and supporting evidence by the specified date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee's affidavit/statement in opposition — timing and service
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 11 days after the day of such delivery the patentee shall leave at the Patent Office his affidavits or statutory declarations in opposition to the petition, and deliver copies to the petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee must file oppositional affidavits within 11 days and provide copies to petitioner; timely compliance is required to preserve procedural rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner’s reply affidavits — timing and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner within 11 days from such delivery shall leave at the Patent Office his affidavits, or statutory declarations in reply, and deliver copies thereof to the patentee; such last-mentioned affidavits or declarations shall be confined to matters strictly in reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies are limited to strictly responsive matters and must be filed and served within 11 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further hearing procedure before Board of Trade
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to any further directions which the Board of Trade may give, the parties shall then be heard at such time, before such person or persons, in such manner, and in accordance with such procedure as the Board of Trade may direct, but so that full opportunity shall be given to the patentee to show cause against the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect directions from the Board about hearing format; ensure opportunity for patentee to present defence is respected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register entry upon sealing of a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the sealing of a patent the Comptroller shall cause to be entered in the register of patents the name, address, and description of the patentee as the grantee thereof, and the title of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accurate name, address, description, and title are supplied for register entry when patent is sealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for entry of proprietor on register after assignment/transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person becomes entitled to a patent or to any share or interest therein by assignment, transmission, or other operation of law, a request for the entry of his name in the register as such proprietor shall be addressed to the Comptroller and left at the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File a formal request at the Patent Office requesting register entry; follow signature/authority requirements (see Rule 69).

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars required in request to be entered on register
rubrics_metrics.description: Such request shall in the case of individuals be signed by the person requiring to be registered or by his duly authorised agent, and shall state the name, address, and description of the claimant and the particulars of the assignment, transmission, or other operation of law, so as to show the manner in which, and the person or persons to whom, the patent or share has been assigned or transmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full particulars of title transfer (dates, parties, nature of instrument) and signature/authority documentation; agents must be authorised to satisfaction of Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production of documents and proof of title for register entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Every assignment and every other document giving effect to, or being evidence of, the transmission of a patent or affecting proprietorship shall be produced to the Comptroller together with the request, and such other proof of title as he may require. For documents which are matters of record, an official or certified copy shall be produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide originals where required, attested copies where allowed, and certified copies for matters of public record. Comptroller may request additional proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attested copy to be left with request
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall also be left with the request an attested copy of the assignment or other document required to be produced; for a document which is a matter of record, an official or certified copy may be left in lieu of an attested copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure an attested copy accompanies the request; use certified copies for records as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate proprietor may be registered by corporate name
rubrics_metrics.description: A body corporate may be registered as proprietor by its corporate name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the proprietor is a corporation, provide corporate name and appropriate evidence of corporate status/authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of Court or Privy Council orders affecting patents/register
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an order has been made by Her Majesty in Council for extension, grant of new patent, revocation, or rectification of the register, the person in whose favour such order has been made shall forthwith leave at the Patent Office an office copy of such order. The register shall be rectified or the purport of such order shall otherwise be duly entered in the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit an office copy of the order promptly to obtain rectification or register entry in accordance with the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of fee payments and failures in Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the issue of a certificate of payment under Rule 48 the Comptroller shall cause to be entered in the Register of Patents a record of the amount and date of payment. If a patentee fails to make any prescribed payment within the prescribed time (or any enlargement duly granted), such failure shall be entered in the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments and failures are publicly recorded. Keep evidence of payments and certificates for register accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing licences for notification in Register
rubrics_metrics.description: An attested copy of every licence granted under a patent shall be left at the Patent Office by the licensee, with a request that a notification thereof may be entered in the register. The licensee shall cause the accuracy of such copy to be certified as the Comptroller may direct, and the original licence shall at the same time be produced and left at the Patent Office if required for further verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide attested copy plus any certification required; produce original if requested for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection hours and exceptions for Register
rubrics_metrics.description: The Register of Patents shall be open to the inspection of the public on every week day between the hours of ten and four, except on specified holidays (Christmas Day, Good Friday, the day observed as Her Majesty's birthday, days of public fast or thanksgiving, Bank of England holidays), days notified by placard, and times when the register is required for official use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public can inspect the register 10:00–16:00 weekdays subject to listed exceptions and placard-notified closures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies and office extracts furnished on payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified copies of any entry in the register, or certified copies of, or extracts from, patents, specifications, disclaimers, affidavits, statutory declarations, and other public documents in the Patent Office, or of or from registers and other books kept there, may be furnished by the Comptroller on payment of the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request certified copies or extracts and pay the prescribed fee; office will supply copies per fee schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to dispense with acts, documents, declarations or evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where under the Rules any person is required to do an act, sign a document, make a declaration, or produce evidence, and it is shown to the satisfaction of the Comptroller that from any reasonable cause such person is unable to do so, it shall be lawful for the Comptroller, with the sanction of the Board of Trade, and upon production of such other evidence and subject to such terms as they may think fit, to dispense with any such act, document, declaration, or evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to Comptroller and produce substitute evidence; Board of Trade sanction and terms may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees schedule — list and amounts for patent office acts
rubrics_metrics.description: First Schedule: detailed list of fees payable on and in connection with letters patent (applications, filings, provisional/complete specifications, appeals, oppositions, hearings, amendments up to and after sealing, compulsory licence applications/oppositions, certificates of renewal, alternative annual fees schedule, charges for enlargement of time, entries, duplicates, notices of exhibition, search/inspection, office copies per 100 words, certifying copies, clerical error corrections, address alterations, and enlargements for filing/acceptance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the First Schedule for precise amounts (e.g., on filing complete specification 3£?00? — see schedule), and alternative annual fee timetable; fees vary by act and by timing (up to sealing/after sealing). Charges apply for enlargements of time (graded by duration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form A: Application for Patent — required content and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Form A (to be accompanied by two Copies of Form B or Form C) requires the applicant's name, full address and calling, declaration of possession of an invention with title, statement of true and first inventor(s), declaration that invention is not in use by others in the UK to the applicant's knowledge, signature(s) of applicant(s), and date. Where an agent is used, an authorisation on the back should be signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and sign Form A; include two copies of provisional or complete specification (Forms B/C); agent authorisation required if using an agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Al/A2: Applications communicated from abroad / priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms Al/A2 for inventions communicated from abroad or under international/colonial arrangements require declaration of communicant, statements that the invention is not in use in the UK, and may include priority details and lists of foreign applications and dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full details of communicant and foreign filing dates; follow priority claim wording and attach supporting documents where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form B: Provisional Specification format and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional Specification (Form B) to be furnished in duplicate; must declare the nature of the invention in a short description; no stamp required; commencement sheet must be signed by applicant or agent with date; continuation on wide-ruled foolscap one side only with two-inch left margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare two duplicate provisional specifications; ensure format (foolscap, margins) and signature/date on first sheet; no stamp needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form C: Complete Specification format, claims phrasing and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete Specification (Form C) to be furnished in duplicate (one unstamped); must contain full description 'in what manner the same is to be performed', and must end with a distinct statement of claim(s) in the form: 'Having now particularly described and ascertained the nature of my said Invention, and in what manner the same is to be performed, I declare that what I claim is: ' followed by the features of novelty claimed. Continuation on foolscap (one side only), two-inch left margin; signed by applicant or agent on last sheet with date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure full descriptive disclosure and clear, distinct claims in the required wording; comply with paper/format/signature rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form D: Opposition to grant — content and unstamped copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Form D (opposition to grant) must be accompanied by an unstamped copy and state the grounds (specifying which of the grounds under section 11 of the Act are relied upon). It must be signed and addressed to the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State statutory grounds of opposition explicitly; provide unstamped copy for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form E: Application for hearing by Comptroller
rubrics_metrics.description: Form E is used to apply to be heard regarding refusal to accept, opposition, or application for amendment, etc., and requests notice of the hearing day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form E when seeking hearing rights before the Comptroller and to obtain notice of hearing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form F: Application to amend specification or drawings — reasons and red-ink copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Form F must state the name and address of applicant/patentee, seek leave to amend the specification as shown in red ink in the copy of the original specification annexed, and set out the reasons for making the amendment (and, where applicant is not the patentee, state the interest possessed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include red-ink marked copy and detailed reasons for amendment; sign Form F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form G: Opposition to amendment form and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Form G for opposition to amendment must be accompanied by an unstamped copy and state the reason of opposition; it must be signed and filed with the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File Form G with unstamped copy and clear statement of grounds for opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms H and HI: Application and petition for compulsory grant of licence — facts and examined copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Form H (application) and Form HI (petition) require the applicant to request that the accompanying petition be brought to Board of Trade notice and that the petition must clearly set forth the facts of the case and be accompanied by an examined copy. Form HI sets out the structure for a petition including details of patent, petitioner's interest, detailed circumstances under section 22, proposed terms, and prayer for relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft petition according to Form HI’s numbered paragraphs; attach examined copy and supporting documentary evidence/affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I: Opposition to compulsory licence application
rubrics_metrics.description: Form I provides a mechanism to give notice of objection to an application for compulsory grant of a licence and is to be addressed to the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form I to lodge opposition; provide particulars and signatures as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form J: Application / certificate of payment or renewal format
rubrics_metrics.description: Form J transmits the prescribed fee for continuation in force of a patent and includes certificate wording to be filled at the Patent Office certifying payment, amount, date, and period of extension of rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form J for payment of renewal fees and to obtain the official certificate of payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form K: Application for enlargement of time for payment of renewal fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Form K must set out application for enlargement of time (specifying the period sought) and state the circumstances in which the payment was omitted (see Rule 49).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed circumstances for omission; fill address for receipt to be sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form L: Request to enter name upon the Register of Patents — content & proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Form L requires the claimant to state name, full address, description, the nature of the claim to the patent, particulars of supporting documents (dates, parties), and to transmit the accompanying examined copy of the document as proof. For matters of record, a certified or official copy may be left in lieu of attested copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach examined copies/certified copies as appropriate when requesting register entry under assignment/transmission claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form M: Request to enter notification of licence in the Register — attested copy & verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Form M transmits an attested copy of a licence granted under a patent and, where required, the original licence for verification, requesting notification entry in the Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure attestation and provide original if asked; request the notification entry in the register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form N: Application for duplicate of Letters Patent — contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Form N requires the applicant to state that the Letters Patent have been destroyed or lost, give particulars (date, number, patentee), and state the applicant's interest in the Letters Patent when applying for a duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain circumstances (lost/destroyed) and evidence of interest when requesting duplicate patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form O: Notice of intended exhibition of an unpatented invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Form O requires the applicant's name and address, notice of intention to exhibit at a specified Exhibition (opened or to open on date), brief description of the invention and drawings if necessary, under provisions of the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act of 1888.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exhibition details, brief description, and drawings where necessary to preserve exhibition rights.
